examples.label: Path-traversal patch to the client's file browser
SQLi UNION payload injected through the client

notes: The client is just a front end to a server API - decompile the jar, patch a request method (path traversal, SQLi), recompile, and the server trusts it. Hardcoded secrets in beans.xml/manifests are common.

recommended.note: Static/behavioral analysis of the same client.

name: Thick Client - Exploit Web Vulns (JAR patch)
command:
# decompile client jar, patch a request method, recompile, run
jar -cmf META-INF/MANIFEST.MF ..\client-new.jar *
description: Java thick clients can be decompiled, modified to inject payloads their UI blocks (path traversal ../../../etc/passwd, SQLi in a field, or client-side password-hash bypass), then recompiled and run against the server.

defense.why_it_works: Thick clients communicating with a web backend are susceptible to the same injection vulnerabilities as web applications. HTTP requests can be intercepted with Burp Suite and modified -- SQL injection, path traversal, and auth bypass work identically to web attacks.
defense.prerequisites: Thick client communicating with a web backend. Ability to proxy traffic through Burp Suite. Backend server vulnerable to injection.
defense.impact: SQL injection leading to credential theft and data exfiltration. Path traversal reading sensitive server files. Authentication bypass gaining higher-privilege access.
defense.detection: Unexpected SQL syntax or traversal sequences in HTTP parameters in web server logs. Database error responses. WAF alert for injection patterns.
defense.artifacts: Web server access log (SQL injection patterns in parameters) | Database error log (syntax errors from injected SQL) | WAF alerts for injection attempts
defense.prevention: Treat thick client HTTP input identically to browser input -- parameterized queries, input validation, WAF. Do not trust client-side validation. Implement server-side session validation.
defense.misconfiguration: Backend web service does not validate or parameterize user-supplied input, assuming the thick client performs all input validation client-side.
